Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১) Which one is vasoconstrictor?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The lungs play an important role in the metabolism and inactivation of vasoactive substances circulating in the blood. Bradykinin is activated/generated in the pulmonary circulation through the action of pulmonary endothelial enzymes, particularly kallikrein-related pathways, while the lungs also rapidly inactivate bradykinin via angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE). In standard exam physiology, the lungs are classically associated with activation of angiotensin I to angiotensin II, but this is actually conversion, not activation of angiotensin I itself. Among the given options, bradykinin is the accepted answer when asking about a substance associated with pulmonary activation/metabolism. Surfactant is produced by type II pneumocytes, while prostaglandins are synthesized in many tissues and are not specifically “activated” in the lung.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • ACE in pulmonary endothelium: Angiotensin I → Angiotensin II.

  • ACE also inactivates bradykinin.

  • Surfactant: produced by type II alveolar pneumocytes.

  • Pulmonary circulation is an important site for metabolism of vasoactive substances.

Exam Pearl:
Remember: Lung + ACE = Angiotensin II formation and Bradykinin degradation.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২) Stable tissues excludes....?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Stable cells (quiescent cells) normally remain in the G₀ phase but can re-enter the cell cycle when stimulated by injury. Examples include parenchymal cells of the liver, kidney, pancreas, smooth muscle cells, and endothelial cells. Transitional epithelium (urothelium) is also capable of regeneration.

Fibroblasts, however, are generally considered labile/stable depending on classification, but in standard pathology MCQs they are commonly grouped with connective tissue cells capable of proliferation rather than as classic stable parenchymal cells. Therefore, among these options, fibroblast is the expected answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Labile: continuously dividing → epidermis, GI epithelium, bone marrow

  • Stable: quiescent but proliferative → liver cells, smooth muscle, endothelium

  • Permanent: minimal/no regeneration → neurons, cardiac myocytes

Exam Pearl:
For classic MCQs, remember liver parenchymal cells = stable cells.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩) Which organ is mainly involved in fat metabolism?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The liver is the principal organ involved in fat (lipid) metabolism. It plays a central role in fatty acid oxidation, synthesis of fatty acids and triglycerides, cholesterol metabolism, and production of lipoproteins. The liver also converts fatty acids into ketone bodies during prolonged fasting or carbohydrate deficiency.

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Liver → major site of lipid metabolism

  • β-oxidation of fatty acids → mainly liver and muscle

  • Ketogenesis → liver

  • Lipoprotein synthesis → liver

Exam Pearl:
For a general MCQ asking the main organ of fat metabolism, choose liver.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪) Granulation tissues are found in.....?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Granulation tissue is a newly formed, highly vascular connective tissue that appears during the proliferative phase of wound healing. It contains numerous newly formed capillaries, proliferating fibroblasts, and inflammatory cells. It is characteristically seen in the floor of a healing ulcer and helps fill the tissue defect before collagen deposition and maturation.

  • Ulcer → granulation tissue commonly present in the floor.

  • Scar → mainly dense, relatively avascular collagen tissue.

  • Keloid → excessive mature collagen deposition.

  • Necrosis → dead tissue, not granulation tissue itself.

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Granulation tissue = capillaries + fibroblasts + inflammatory cells

  • Commonly seen in healing wounds/ulcers

  • Later matures into scar tissue

Exam Pearl:
“Ulcer floor → granulation tissue.”

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫) Affected tissues turn red in.....?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Hyperemia হলো কোনো টিস্যুতে arterial blood flow বৃদ্ধি পাওয়া, যার ফলে আক্রান্ত টিস্যুতে বেশি অক্সিজেনযুক্ত রক্ত জমা হয় এবং টিস্যু লাল (red) ও উষ্ণ দেখায়। এটি সাধারণত active process এবং arteriolar dilation-এর কারণে হয়।

  • Hyperemia → red, warm tissue

  • Congestion → bluish-red/cyanotic, venous outflow বাধাগ্রস্ত হওয়ার কারণে

  • Oedema → fluid accumulation

  • Shock → systemic tissue hypoperfusion

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Hyperemia = Active + arterial dilation + red

  • Congestion = Passive + venous obstruction + blue-red

  • Rubor (redness) is a classic feature of inflammation.

Exam Pearl:
Hyperemia = increased arterial blood flow → redness.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬) Embryonic hemoglobin excludes…?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Embryonic hemoglobins are produced during the embryonic period (approximately up to 8–10 weeks of gestation). The major embryonic hemoglobins are:

  • Hb Gower I = ζ₂ε₂

  • Hb Gower II = α₂ε₂

  • Hb Portland = ζ₂γ₂

Hb Bart's (γ₄) is not an embryonic hemoglobin. It is a fetal hemoglobin variant, particularly associated with α-thalassemia major (Hb Bart's hydrops fetalis).

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Embryonic: Gower I, Gower II, Portland

  • Fetal: HbF = α₂γ₂

  • Hb Bart's: γ₄ → severe α-thalassemia

Exam Pearl:
Remember: “Gower + Portland = embryonic; Bart’s = α-thalassemia.”

উত্তর: ক) Hb Barts

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭) Which operation protects ulcerative colitis but increases the risk of Crohn's disease?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Appendicectomy is associated with a reduced risk of developing ulcerative colitis (UC), particularly when performed at a young age. However, this protective association is not seen for Crohn’s disease; some studies have found an increased subsequent risk of Crohn’s disease after appendicectomy, although the relationship is complex and may partly reflect diagnostic bias.

  • Appendicectomy → ↓ risk of UC

  • Appendicectomy → associated with ↑ risk of Crohn’s disease

  • Cholecystectomy does not have this classic association.

  • Ileostomy/colostomy are treatments or surgical procedures rather than the classic answer to this epidemiological association.

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Appendicectomy → protective against UC

  • Appendicectomy is not protective against Crohn’s disease

  • UC: continuous colonic inflammation

  • Crohn’s: skip lesions, transmural inflammation

Exam Pearl:
A classic exam association is: “Appendicectomy → ↓ UC risk.”

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮) What is the main source of arterial supply in pancreas?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The main arterial supply of the pancreas comes from branches of the splenic artery, particularly for the body and tail. Important branches include the dorsal pancreatic, great pancreatic, and caudal pancreatic arteries. The head of the pancreas is supplied by the pancreaticoduodenal arcades, which receive blood from both the superior pancreaticoduodenal artery (from the gastroduodenal artery) and inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery (from the SMA).

Therefore, among the given options, the branches of the splenic artery are the main source.

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Body & tail → splenic artery branches

  • Head → superior + inferior pancreaticoduodenal arteries

  • Splenic artery → major arterial supply of pancreas

Exam Pearl:
For a single-best-answer MCQ asking the main source of pancreatic arterial supply, choose splenic artery branches.

উত্তর: গ) Branches of splenic artery

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯) Which is pathognomonic radiological sign of Crohn's disease ?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The String sign of Kantor is a classic radiological sign of Crohn’s disease, especially involving the terminal ileum. It results from marked luminal narrowing due to transmural inflammation, edema, and fibrosis, allowing only a thin stream of contrast to pass through the affected segment—giving the appearance of a string.

  • String sign → Crohn’s disease

  • Whirlpool sign → volvulus

  • Double bubble sign → duodenal atresia

  • Ribbon sign → not the classic sign of Crohn’s disease

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Crohn’s → String sign

  • Crohn’s → Skip lesions, cobblestone appearance

  • UC → Lead-pipe appearance

  • Crohn’s commonly affects the terminal ileum

Exam Pearl:
“Crohn’s = String sign” is a high-yield radiology association.

উত্তর: খ) String sign

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১০) Which is activated in lung?
১১) What is the nature of pain in PUD?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Pain in peptic ulcer disease (PUD) is classically described as a burning or gnawing epigastric pain. The pain is related to gastric acid and peptic activity at the ulcer site. In duodenal ulcer, pain typically occurs 2–5 hours after meals or at night and may be relieved by food or antacids. In gastric ulcer, pain may occur shortly after eating and can be worsened by food. Spasmodic or colicky pain suggests hollow-viscus obstruction or intestinal smooth-muscle spasm, while throbbing pain is more characteristic of vascular or inflammatory processes. Therefore, among the given options, burning is the best description.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • PUD pain: burning/gnawing epigastric pain

  • Duodenal ulcer: classically relieved by food

  • Gastric ulcer: classically may worsen with food

  • Antacids often provide temporary relief.

Exam Pearl:
PUD → burning/gnawing epigastric pain.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১২) Which one synthesizes intracytoplasmic protein?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Ribosomes are the primary site of intracytoplasmic protein synthesis. They translate messenger RNA (mRNA) into polypeptide chains by linking amino acids together. Free ribosomes in the cytoplasm synthesize proteins that function within the cytosol, nucleus, mitochondria, and peroxisomes. Rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) contains ribosomes attached to its surface and is involved in the synthesis and processing of proteins destined for secretion, lysosomes, or cell membranes. Smooth ER is mainly involved in lipid synthesis and detoxification, while lysosomes contain digestive enzymes for intracellular degradation. Therefore, the direct answer for intracytoplasmic protein synthesis is ribosome.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Ribosome: site of translation and protein synthesis.

  • Free ribosomes: synthesize cytoplasmic proteins.

  • Rough ER: synthesizes secretory and membrane proteins due to attached ribosomes.

  • Smooth ER: lipid synthesis, steroid synthesis, detoxification.

  • Lysosome: intracellular digestion.

Exam Pearl:
Ribosome = the universal machinery for protein synthesis.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৩) Which one is gold standard for H. Pylori?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
This question is ambiguous because the term "gold standard" depends on the context. If the question asks for the definitive diagnostic (gold standard) test, the answer is culture of gastric biopsy specimens (with histology often considered alongside it), as culture provides direct identification of Helicobacter pylori and allows antibiotic susceptibility testing. However, culture is technically demanding and is not routinely used in clinical practice. Urea breath test is the best non-invasive test for detecting active infection and confirming eradication. Rapid urease test is an accurate invasive biopsy-based test but is not the gold standard. Serology detects antibodies and cannot distinguish active from past infection.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Culture (gastric biopsy): Definitive diagnosis; allows antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

  • Urea breath test: Best non-invasive test for active infection and post-treatment confirmation.

  • Rapid urease test: Biopsy-based, rapid, highly specific.

  • Serology: Not suitable for confirming eradication.

Exam Pearl:
Remember the distinction:

  • Gold standard (definitive): Culture of gastric biopsy.

  • Best non-invasive test: Urea breath test.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৪) Feature of hypercapnia includes….?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Hypercapnia (elevated arterial PaCO₂) causes CO₂ narcosis, cerebral vasodilation, and depression of the central nervous system. One of the characteristic neurological signs is asterixis (flapping tremor), which results from impaired motor control due to hypercapnic encephalopathy. Patients may also present with headache, confusion, drowsiness, warm flushed skin, bounding pulse, and, in severe cases, coma. Cold peripheries, rapid thready pulse, and hypotension are more suggestive of shock or poor peripheral perfusion rather than uncomplicated hypercapnia. Therefore, flapping tremor is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hypercapnia: PaCO₂ > 45 mmHg.

  • Features: Headache, confusion, drowsiness, asterixis (flapping tremor), CO₂ narcosis.

  • Severe hypercapnia can progress to respiratory acidosis and coma.

  • Common causes: COPD exacerbation, hypoventilation, neuromuscular disorders, CNS depression.

Exam Pearl:
Think hypercapnia = CO₂ retention = asterixis (flapping tremor) + drowsiness + respiratory acidosis.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৫) What is the nature of breath sound in a patient with bronchial asthma?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
In bronchial asthma, the breath sound is typically vesicular with prolonged expiration. Airway inflammation, bronchial smooth muscle constriction, and mucus plugging increase airway resistance, particularly during expiration, leading to prolonged expiratory time. Wheeze, a high-pitched continuous musical sound, is the characteristic added sound, especially during expiration. The basic breath sound remains vesicular unless there is associated lung consolidation. Bronchial breath sounds are normally heard over the trachea and are pathological when heard over peripheral lung fields, usually indicating lung consolidation (e.g., pneumonia), not asthma.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Asthma: Vesicular breath sounds with prolonged expiration.

  • Wheeze: Hallmark auscultatory finding, predominantly expiratory.

  • Severe asthma ("silent chest"): Markedly diminished breath sounds due to minimal airflow.

  • Bronchial breath sounds: Suggest lung consolidation, not bronchial asthma.

Exam Pearl:
Asthma = expiratory wheeze + prolonged expiration with vesicular breath sounds.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৬) Which is example of simple alveolar exocrine gland?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A simple alveolar (acinar) exocrine gland consists of a single, unbranched duct that ends in a rounded secretory sac (alveolus/acinus). The sebaceous gland is the classic example of a simple branched alveolar gland and is the accepted answer in most anatomy MCQs when "simple alveolar gland" is listed. It secretes sebum by holocrine secretion into hair follicles. In contrast, sweat glands are simple coiled tubular glands, mammary glands are compound tubuloalveolar glands, and major salivary glands are compound tubuloacinar (tubuloalveolar) glands.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Sebaceous gland: Simple branched alveolar (acinar); holocrine secretion.

  • Sweat gland (eccrine): Simple coiled tubular.

  • Mammary gland: Compound tubuloalveolar.

  • Salivary glands: Compound tubuloacinar (tubuloalveolar).

Exam Pearl:
Sebaceous gland is the classic example of an alveolar (acinar) exocrine gland and secretes by the holocrine mechanism.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৭) What is the commonest organism for hospital acquired pneumonia?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP) is pneumonia that develops 48 hours or more after hospital admission and was not incubating at the time of admission. The most common causative organisms are Gram-negative bacilli, particularly Pseudomonas aeruginosa, especially in critically ill, ventilated, or immunocompromised patients. Staphylococcus aureus (including MRSA) is also a major cause of HAP but is less common than Gram-negative organisms overall. In contrast, Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae are more frequently associated with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP).

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • HAP: Occurs ≥48 hours after hospital admission.

  • Common pathogens: Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella, E. coli, Acinetobacter, MRSA.

  • Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is a subtype of HAP developing ≥48 hours after endotracheal intubation.

  • Empiric therapy should cover Pseudomonas and MRSA when risk factors are present.

Exam Pearl:
For HAP, think Gram-negative bacilli first—especially Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৮) TV+IRV=?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Inspiratory Capacity (IC) is the maximum volume of air that can be inspired after a normal tidal expiration. It is the sum of Tidal Volume (TV) and Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV):

IC = TV + IRV

This represents the total amount of air that can be inhaled starting from the end of a normal expiration. By contrast, Functional Residual Capacity (FRC) = ERV + RV, Vital Capacity (VC) = IRV + TV + ERV, and Total Lung Capacity (TLC) = VC + RV.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • IC = TV + IRV

  • VC = IRV + TV + ERV

  • FRC = ERV + RV

  • TLC = IRV + TV + ERV + RV = VC + RV

  • Residual Volume (RV) cannot be measured by simple spirometry.

Exam Pearl:
Memorize the basic formula: Inspiratory Capacity = Tidal Volume + Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IC = TV + IRV).

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৯) If large amount of fluid is aspirated at a time there may be......?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
This question refers to therapeutic thoracentesis (pleural fluid aspiration). If a large volume of pleural fluid is removed rapidly, the patient may develop re-expansion pulmonary oedema (RPE). This occurs because the previously collapsed lung re-expands suddenly, leading to increased pulmonary capillary permeability and leakage of fluid into the alveoli. RPE is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication. To minimize this risk, it is generally recommended not to remove more than 1–1.5 liters of pleural fluid at one time unless pleural pressure is being monitored. Pneumothorax is a procedural complication but is not specifically related to aspirating a large volume of fluid.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Large-volume thoracentesis may cause re-expansion pulmonary oedema.

  • Limit pleural fluid removal to 1–1.5 L in a single session (without pleural pressure monitoring).

  • Pneumothorax is the most common procedural complication.

  • Symptoms of RPE: dyspnea, cough, hypoxemia, and new unilateral pulmonary infiltrates.

Exam Pearl:
Rapid removal of a large volume of pleural fluid → Re-expansion pulmonary oedema.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২০) Sarcoma usually follows....route?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Sarcomas are malignant tumors arising from mesenchymal tissues such as bone, muscle, fat, cartilage, and connective tissue. They characteristically metastasize via the hematogenous (bloodstream) route, with the lungs being the most common site of distant metastasis. In contrast, carcinomas usually spread first through the lymphatic system to regional lymph nodes. Although advanced sarcomas can occasionally involve lymph nodes or spread by direct seeding, these are uncommon and not the typical route of dissemination. Therefore, the most accepted and best answer is hematogenous spread.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Sarcoma → Hematogenous spread → Lungs (most common metastatic site).

  • Carcinoma → Lymphatic spread → Regional lymph nodes.

  • Lymph node metastasis is rare in most sarcomas.

  • Exceptions with relatively higher lymphatic spread include rhabdomyosarcoma, synovial sarcoma, epithelioid sarcoma, and clear cell sarcoma.

Exam Pearl:
Remember: Sarcoma spreads through blood; Carcinoma spreads through lymphatics.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২১) Which is not a feature of left suprarenal gland?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The left suprarenal (adrenal) gland is semilunar (crescent-shaped), whereas the right suprarenal gland is pyramidal. Therefore, describing the left adrenal gland as pyramidal is incorrect. Anatomically, the left suprarenal gland lies anteromedial to the upper pole of the left kidney. Its anterior surface is related to the stomach (through the lesser sac) and the pancreas, while its medial border is related to the coeliac ganglion. The hilum, through which the suprarenal vein emerges, is situated near the lower part of the gland.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Right suprarenal gland: Pyramidal.

  • Left suprarenal gland: Semilunar (crescent-shaped).

  • Right suprarenal vein drains directly into the IVC.

  • Left suprarenal vein drains into the left renal vein.

Exam Pearl:
Shape is the easiest differentiator: Right adrenal = pyramidal; Left adrenal = semilunar.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২২) Which of the following is not a mechanisms for reducing blood glucose level by insulin?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).option1: Increases transport and uptake of glucose by the cells
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Insulin lowers blood glucose by facilitating glucose uptake into skeletal muscle and adipose tissue through GLUT-4 transporters, increasing peripheral glucose utilization, inhibiting hepatic gluconeogenesis, and stimulating glycogenesis (conversion of glucose to glycogen) in the liver and skeletal muscle. Therefore, the statement "inhibits glycogenesis" is incorrect. In fact, insulin has the opposite effect—it promotes glycogenesis while inhibiting glycogenolysis, thereby reducing blood glucose levels.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Insulin increases GLUT-4–mediated glucose uptake in muscle and adipose tissue.

  • Stimulates glycogenesis.

  • Inhibits glycogenolysis.

  • Inhibits gluconeogenesis.

  • Promotes lipogenesis and protein synthesis.

Exam Pearl:
Insulin promotes glycogenesis—not inhibits it. If you see "inhibits glycogenesis," it is the incorrect option.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৩) T-wave in ECG indicates…?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The T wave on the electrocardiogram (ECG) represents ventricular repolarization, the process by which ventricular myocardial cells return to their resting electrical state after depolarization and contraction. Although repolarization is an electrical recovery process, it occurs while the ventricles are still mechanically contracting. Atrial repolarization does occur but is normally hidden within the QRS complex because ventricular depolarization generates a much larger electrical signal. Therefore, the T wave specifically reflects ventricular repolarization.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • P wave: Atrial depolarization.

  • QRS complex: Ventricular depolarization.

  • T wave: Ventricular repolarization.

  • Atrial repolarization: Obscured by the QRS complex.

  • QT interval: Represents total ventricular electrical activity (depolarization + repolarization).

Exam Pearl:
ECG sequence to remember: P = Atrial depolarization, QRS = Ventricular depolarization, T = Ventricular repolarization.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৪) Which one is the most active adrenal androgen?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The adrenal cortex (mainly the zona reticularis) secretes dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), DHEA sulfate (DHEAS), and androstenedione, which are relatively weak androgens. Testosterone is the most biologically active androgen among the options, although it is produced predominantly by the testes (and in smaller amounts by the ovaries and peripheral conversion), not directly by the adrenal cortex in significant amounts. Therefore, the question is slightly ambiguous. If it asks for the most active androgen among the listed options, the correct answer is testosterone. If it intended the major adrenal androgen, the answer would be DHEA (or DHEAS if listed).

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Zona reticularis secretes DHEA, DHEAS, and androstenedione.

  • DHEAS is the major circulating adrenal androgen.

  • Testosterone is the most potent naturally occurring androgen.

  • Peripheral conversion of adrenal androgens contributes to testosterone and estrogen production.

Exam Pearl:
Most active androgen = Testosterone; Major adrenal androgen = DHEA/DHEAS.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৫) Which is example of serum sicknesses?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
This question is ambiguous because serum sickness is the classic example of a Type III (immune complex-mediated) hypersensitivity reaction, but "serum sickness" itself is not listed as an option. Among the given choices, Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is the best answer because it is a prototypical Type III hypersensitivity disease, in which circulating antigen–antibody immune complexes deposit in tissues, activating complement and causing inflammation and tissue damage. Farmer's lung is also a Type III hypersensitivity reaction (hypersensitivity pneumonitis), but it is not serum sickness. Cystic fibrosis is a genetic disorder, and granuloma is typically associated with Type IV (delayed) hypersensitivity.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Type III hypersensitivity: Immune complex-mediated.

  • Classic examples: Serum sickness, SLE, post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, Arthus reaction.

  • Farmer's lung: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis (predominantly Type III, with some Type IV involvement).

  • Granuloma: Characteristic of Type IV hypersensitivity.

Exam Pearl:
Serum sickness and SLE are classic Type III hypersensitivity disorders caused by immune complex deposition.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৬) Which is not a congenital diaphragmatic hernia?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Congenital diaphragmatic hernias (CDH) are developmental defects of the diaphragm present at birth. The main types are posterolateral (Bochdalek hernia), which is the most common, retrosternal (Morgagni hernia), and the rarer central diaphragmatic defects. In contrast, a hiatal hernia is a herniation of the stomach through the esophageal hiatus. Although rare congenital forms exist, hiatal hernia is generally considered an acquired condition in adults and is not classified as a congenital diaphragmatic hernia in standard anatomy and surgical examinations. Therefore, among the given options, hiatal hernia is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Bochdalek hernia: Posterolateral; most common CDH; usually left-sided.

  • Morgagni hernia: Retrosternal (anteromedial); less common.

  • Central diaphragmatic defect: Rare congenital type.

  • Hiatal hernia: Usually acquired; involves the esophageal hiatus.

Exam Pearl:
Congenital diaphragmatic hernia = Bochdalek (posterolateral), Morgagni (retrosternal), or central defect—not hiatal hernia.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৭) Hyperthyroidism in women leads to....?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Hyperthyroidism commonly causes menstrual disturbances, with oligomenorrhea (infrequent menstrual periods) being the most characteristic finding. Excess thyroid hormones alter the hypothalamic–pituitary–ovarian axis, affecting gonadotropin secretion and estrogen metabolism, which leads to menstrual irregularities and may reduce fertility. In severe cases, amenorrhea may occur. In contrast, hypothyroidism is more commonly associated with menorrhagia due to anovulation and altered coagulation factors. Therefore, among the given options, oligomenorrhea is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hyperthyroidism: Oligomenorrhea, amenorrhea, reduced fertility.

  • Hypothyroidism: Menorrhagia, menstrual irregularities.

  • Thyroid dysfunction can cause anovulation.

  • Correcting thyroid disease often restores normal menstrual cycles.

Exam Pearl:
Hyperthyroidism → Oligomenorrhea; Hypothyroidism → Menorrhagia.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৮) Clotting factor number…… is also called proaccelerin?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Factor V is also known as Proaccelerin or the Labile factor. It is synthesized mainly in the liver and functions as a cofactor in the common pathway of the coagulation cascade. Activated Factor V (Va) combines with Factor Xa, calcium, and phospholipids to form the prothrombinase complex, which converts prothrombin (Factor II) into thrombin (Factor IIa). Factor VI is an obsolete term and is no longer recognized as a separate clotting factor; it was later identified as activated Factor V. Factor VII is Proconvertin, and Factor VIII is the Anti-hemophilic factor A.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Factor V = Proaccelerin (Labile factor).

  • Factor VII = Proconvertin (Stable factor).

  • Factor VIII = Anti-hemophilic factor A.

  • Factor VI is obsolete; it represents activated Factor V (Va).

  • Factor V deficiency causes prolonged PT and aPTT.

Exam Pearl:
Proaccelerin = Factor V; there is no separate Factor VI in the modern coagulation factor nomenclature.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৯) Which one is the most common bacterial cause of sore throat?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The most common bacterial cause of acute pharyngitis (sore throat) is Group A β-hemolytic Streptococcus (GAS), Streptococcus pyogenes. Although most cases of sore throat are viral, S. pyogenes is the most common bacterial pathogen, particularly in school-aged children (5–15 years). Patients typically present with sudden-onset sore throat, fever, tonsillar exudates, tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy, and absence of cough. Prompt diagnosis and treatment are important to prevent acute rheumatic fever and other suppurative complications. Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, and Staphylococcus epidermidis are not common causes of uncomplicated bacterial pharyngitis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common overall cause of sore throat: Viruses.

  • Most common bacterial cause: Group A β-hemolytic Streptococcus (S. pyogenes).

  • Diagnosis: Rapid antigen detection test (RADT) or throat culture.

  • Complications: Acute rheumatic fever, peritonsillar abscess, post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis.

Exam Pearl:
Remember: Viral is the commonest overall cause of sore throat, but Streptococcus pyogenes is the commonest bacterial cause.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩০) Acrodermatitis enteropathica is caused by deficiency of......?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Acrodermatitis enteropathica is a rare disorder caused by zinc deficiency, most commonly due to an inherited defect in the SLC39A4 gene, which impairs intestinal zinc absorption. It may also occur as an acquired condition from inadequate dietary intake or malabsorption. The classic triad includes periorificial and acral dermatitis, alopecia, and diarrhea. Other features include growth retardation, impaired wound healing, recurrent infections, and altered taste. Diagnosis is supported by low serum zinc levels, and treatment with oral zinc supplementation produces a rapid and dramatic clinical response.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Acrodermatitis enteropathica = Zinc deficiency.

  • Classic triad: Dermatitis + Diarrhea + Alopecia.

  • Inherited form: Autosomal recessive, due to SLC39A4 mutation.

  • Treatment: Lifelong oral zinc supplementation in the inherited form.

Exam Pearl:
Think "3 Ds" of zinc deficiency: Dermatitis, Diarrhea, and (hair loss) Alopecia.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩১) Which one is also called nexus?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A gap junction is also called a nexus. It is a specialized intercellular junction that allows direct communication between adjacent cells by permitting the passage of ions and small molecules through channels formed by connexons (made of connexin proteins). Gap junctions are essential for electrical and metabolic coupling, particularly in cardiac muscle, smooth muscle, and some epithelial tissues, enabling coordinated cellular activity. In contrast, tight junctions (zonula occludens) prevent paracellular leakage, desmosomes (macula adherens) provide strong cell-to-cell adhesion, and hemidesmosomes anchor epithelial cells to the basement membrane.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Gap junction = Nexus.

  • Formed by connexons, composed of connexins.

  • Permits passage of ions and small molecules (<1 kDa).

  • Important in cardiac muscle and smooth muscle for electrical coupling.

  • Tight junction: Barrier function.

  • Desmosome: Cell-to-cell mechanical adhesion.

  • Hemidesmosome: Cell-to-basement membrane attachment.

Exam Pearl:
Nexus = Gap junction = Direct intercellular communication via connexons.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩২) Which of the following causes infection of prosthetic heart bulb & hip?
৩৩) PT is normal in….?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Prothrombin time (PT) assesses the extrinsic and common coagulation pathways, primarily involving Factors VII, X, V, II (prothrombin), and fibrinogen. In hemophilia A (Factor VIII deficiency) and hemophilia B (Factor IX deficiency), the defect is in the intrinsic pathway, so PT remains normal, while activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) is prolonged. In contrast, liver disease reduces synthesis of multiple clotting factors, causing prolonged PT. Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) consumes clotting factors, prolonging both PT and aPTT. Anticoagulant therapy with warfarin primarily prolongs PT/INR.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • PT: Assesses extrinsic (Factor VII) and common pathways.

  • aPTT: Assesses intrinsic (Factors XII, XI, IX, VIII) and common pathways.

  • Hemophilia A: Factor VIII deficiency → Normal PT, prolonged aPTT.

  • Hemophilia B: Factor IX deficiency → Normal PT, prolonged aPTT.

  • Warfarin: Prolongs PT/INR.

  • DIC: Prolongs both PT and aPTT.

Exam Pearl:
Hemophilia affects the intrinsic pathway—PT is normal, while aPTT is prolonged.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৪) Which one is a feature of Type-1 DM?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).option2: history of other autoimmune disease uncommon
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is an autoimmune disorder characterized by T-cell–mediated destruction of pancreatic β-cells, resulting in absolute insulin deficiency. It most commonly presents in children, adolescents, and young adults, although it can occur at any age. Patients are usually lean, and there is often a personal or family history of other autoimmune diseases such as autoimmune thyroid disease or celiac disease. A strong family history of diabetes is less common than in Type 2 diabetes. Therefore, among the given options, the characteristic feature of T1DM is that it usually occurs in young people.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Type 1 DM: Autoimmune β-cell destruction.

  • Usually presents in children and adolescents.

  • Absolute insulin deficiency → lifelong insulin therapy.

  • Associated with HLA-DR3 and HLA-DR4.

  • Increased risk of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA).

  • Frequently associated with other autoimmune diseases.

Exam Pearl:
Type 1 DM = Young, lean, autoimmune, insulin-dependent, and prone to DKA.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৫) Which blotting technique for RNA analysis?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Northern blotting is the technique used for the detection and analysis of RNA, particularly mRNA, allowing assessment of gene expression. RNA samples are separated by gel electrophoresis, transferred to a membrane, and hybridized with a labeled complementary nucleic acid probe. In contrast, Southern blotting detects DNA, while Western blotting detects proteins using specific antibodies. Northwestern blotting is a specialized technique used to identify RNA-binding proteins, not RNA itself. Therefore, the correct answer is Northern blot.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Southern blot → DNA

  • Northern blot → RNA

  • Western blot → Protein

  • Southwestern blot → DNA-binding proteins

  • Northwestern blot → RNA-binding proteins

  • Eastern blot → Detection of post-translational protein modifications (e.g., glycosylation).

Exam Pearl:
Mnemonic: "SNoW DRoP"

  • Southern → DNA

  • Northern → RNA

  • Western → Protein

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৬) Tributaries of inferior vena cava excludes…?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The inferior vena cava (IVC) is formed by the union of the right and left common iliac veins and receives several major tributaries, including the hepatic veins, renal veins, right suprarenal vein, inferior phrenic veins, and gonadal veins (the right gonadal vein drains directly into the IVC). The left suprarenal vein is an exception because it does not drain directly into the IVC. Instead, it drains into the left renal vein, which subsequently empties into the IVC. Therefore, among the given options, left suprarenal vein is not a direct tributary of the IVC.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • IVC is formed by the common iliac veins (L5 level).

  • Direct tributaries: Hepatic veins, renal veins, right suprarenal vein, right gonadal vein.

  • Left suprarenal vein → Left renal vein → IVC.

  • Left gonadal vein → Left renal vein → IVC.

Exam Pearl:
Right suprarenal and right gonadal veins drain directly into the IVC, whereas the left-sided counterparts drain into the left renal vein.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৭) Which jerk is affected in hypothyroidism?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A characteristic neurological finding in hypothyroidism is delayed relaxation of deep tendon reflexes, also called hung-up reflexes. This is most prominently observed in the ankle jerk (Achilles tendon reflex). The delayed relaxation results from impaired calcium reuptake by the sarcoplasmic reticulum in skeletal muscle due to reduced thyroid hormone levels. Although other deep tendon reflexes may also be affected, the ankle jerk is the classic and most commonly tested finding. Jaw jerk and plantar reflex are not characteristic abnormalities in hypothyroidism.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hypothyroidism: Delayed relaxation ("hung-up") of ankle jerk.

  • Mechanism: Decreased thyroid hormone → slowed muscle relaxation.

  • Other features: Fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, constipation, bradycardia.

  • Hyperthyroidism: Brisk deep tendon reflexes.

Exam Pearl:
Hung-up ankle jerk is a classic clinical sign of hypothyroidism.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৮) Which digestive juice contains maximum solid component among all?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Among the major digestive secretions, bile contains the highest concentration of solid components (approximately 3–8% solids). These solids are mainly bile salts, phospholipids (especially lecithin), cholesterol, bilirubin, proteins, and electrolytes. Although bile contains no digestive enzymes, it plays a crucial role in fat emulsification and facilitates the absorption of fat and fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, and K). Pancreatic juice, saliva, and succus entericus are predominantly water (>98%) and contain a lower proportion of dissolved solids than bile.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Bile: Highest solid content among digestive juices.

  • Bile contains bile salts, bilirubin, cholesterol, lecithin, and electrolytes.

  • Bile has no digestive enzymes.

  • Pancreatic juice: Rich in digestive enzymes and bicarbonate.

  • Succus entericus: Intestinal secretion containing mucus and brush-border enzymes.

Exam Pearl:
Bile is the digestive secretion with the highest solid content, despite containing no digestive enzymes.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৯) What type of carditis is seen in acute rheumatic fever?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Acute rheumatic fever (ARF) characteristically causes pancarditis, meaning inflammation of all three layers of the heart: the endocardium, myocardium, and pericardium. This is one of the major Jones criteria for the diagnosis of ARF. Endocarditis primarily affects the heart valves (especially the mitral valve, followed by the aortic valve), myocarditis is characterized by Aschoff bodies and may lead to heart failure, while pericarditis produces a fibrinous ("bread-and-butter") pericarditis. Since all three layers are involved simultaneously, the correct term is pancarditis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • ARF carditis = Pancarditis.

  • Endocarditis: Valvulitis, especially mitral valve.

  • Myocarditis: Aschoff bodies are pathognomonic.

  • Pericarditis: Fibrinous ("bread-and-butter") pericarditis.

  • Carditis is a major Jones criterion.

Exam Pearl:
Acute rheumatic fever affects the entire heart—remember "Pancarditis = Endocarditis + Myocarditis + Pericarditis."

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪০) Which cannot penetrate skin?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Loa loa does not penetrate intact skin. It is transmitted to humans through the bite of the Chrysops (deer fly), which deposits infective larvae during feeding. In contrast, Ancylostoma duodenale and Necator americanus (hookworms) infect humans by direct penetration of intact skin, usually through bare feet. Larva migrans (most commonly caused by dog and cat hookworms such as Ancylostoma braziliense) also results from skin penetration by infective larvae, producing serpiginous cutaneous tracks. Therefore, Loa loa is the only option that does not infect by skin penetration.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Ancylostoma duodenale → Skin penetration.

  • Necator americanus → Skin penetration.

  • Cutaneous larva migrans → Skin penetration by animal hookworm larvae.

  • Loa loa → Transmitted by Chrysops (deer fly) bite.

  • Wuchereria bancrofti → Mosquito vector.

Exam Pearl:
Hookworms penetrate skin; Loa loa is vector-borne via the Chrysops fly and does not penetrate intact skin directly.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪১) Sympathetic supply of stomach is derived from…..?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The sympathetic innervation of the stomach arises from the T6–T10 spinal cord segments. Preganglionic sympathetic fibers travel through the greater thoracic splanchnic nerves to the celiac ganglion, where they synapse. Postganglionic fibers then accompany branches of the celiac trunk to reach the stomach. Sympathetic stimulation causes vasoconstriction, decreased gastric motility and secretion, and contraction of sphincters. In contrast, the parasympathetic supply to the stomach is provided by the vagus nerve (CN X), which increases gastric motility and secretion.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Sympathetic supply of stomach: T6–T10 via greater splanchnic nerves.

  • Synapse occurs in the celiac ganglion.

  • Parasympathetic supply: Vagus nerve (CN X).

  • Sympathetic stimulation ↓ gastric motility and secretion; parasympathetic stimulation ↑ both.

Exam Pearl:
Stomach: Sympathetic = T6–T10 (greater splanchnic → celiac ganglion); Parasympathetic = Vagus nerve.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪২) All of the following are causes of right heart failure except....?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Right heart failure is commonly caused by conditions that increase pulmonary artery pressure or produce right ventricular volume overload. Mitral stenosis (MS) increases left atrial pressure, leading to pulmonary hypertension and eventually right ventricular failure. Atrial septal defect (ASD) and ventricular septal defect (VSD) produce left-to-right shunts, causing chronic pulmonary overcirculation that may progress to pulmonary hypertension and right heart failure (or Eisenmenger syndrome). Aortic stenosis (AS) primarily causes left ventricular pressure overload and left-sided heart failure. Although advanced AS can secondarily affect the right heart, it is not a typical direct cause of right heart failure.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Common causes of right heart failure:

    • Pulmonary hypertension (cor pulmonale)

    • Mitral stenosis

    • ASD and VSD (via pulmonary hypertension)

    • Pulmonary valve disease

  • Aortic stenosis mainly causes left ventricular hypertrophy and left-sided heart failure.

Exam Pearl:
Think: Right heart failure results from pulmonary hypertension or right ventricular overload. Aortic stenosis is primarily a cause of left heart failure.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৩) Which transporter play role in basal glucose uptake?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The question is slightly ambiguous because basal glucose uptake in most tissues is primarily mediated by GLUT1, which is not listed among the options. Therefore, the question is flawed. Among the given choices, GLUT3 is the closest and best answer because it is a high-affinity, insulin-independent glucose transporter responsible for continuous glucose uptake in neurons, even at low blood glucose concentrations.

  • GLUT4 is insulin-dependent and is found in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue.

  • GLUT5 transports fructose, not glucose.

  • GLUT6 has no major established role in basal glucose uptake.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • GLUT1: Basal glucose uptake; RBCs, blood-brain barrier, placenta.

  • GLUT2: Liver, pancreatic β-cells, kidney, intestine; low-affinity, high-capacity.

  • GLUT3: Neurons; very high affinity for glucose.

  • GLUT4: Insulin-dependent; skeletal muscle and adipose tissue.

  • GLUT5: Fructose transporter.

Exam Pearl:
Basal glucose uptake = GLUT1. If GLUT1 is absent from the options, choose GLUT3 as the best available insulin-independent glucose transporter.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৪) Middle part of ureter doesn’t receive blood supply from which vessel?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The ureter receives a segmental blood supply from different arteries along its course. The upper ureter is supplied by branches of the renal artery (and occasionally directly from the abdominal aorta). The middle ureter is supplied mainly by the gonadal (testicular/ovarian) arteries, common iliac artery, and branches of the abdominal aorta-derived vessels such as the colic arteries. The lower ureter receives blood from branches of the internal iliac artery (e.g., superior vesical, inferior vesical, uterine, and middle rectal arteries).

Among the given options, the middle part does not receive a direct blood supply from the abdominal aorta. Therefore, Aorta is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Upper ureter: Renal artery.

  • Middle ureter: Gonadal, common iliac, and colic branches.

  • Lower ureter: Internal iliac branches (superior vesical, uterine/inferior vesical).

  • Ureteric arteries form a longitudinal anastomotic network.

Exam Pearl:
Remember the ureter's blood supply is segmental: Upper = renal, Middle = gonadal/common iliac, Lower = internal iliac.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৫) Which causes Chagas disease?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Chagas disease (American trypanosomiasis) is caused by Trypanosoma cruzi, a protozoan parasite transmitted primarily by the triatomine (reduviid or "kissing") bug. Infection occurs when parasite-containing bug feces contaminate the bite wound or mucous membranes. Acute infection may present with Romaña sign (unilateral periorbital swelling) or a chagoma. Chronic disease can lead to dilated cardiomyopathy, arrhythmias, megaesophagus, and megacolon due to destruction of the autonomic nervous system. The other organisms listed cause different diseases: Plasmodium causes malaria, Leishmania causes leishmaniasis, and Giardia causes giardiasis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Chagas disease: Trypanosoma cruzi.

  • Vector: Triatomine (kissing/reduviid) bug.

  • Acute feature: Romaña sign.

  • Chronic complications: Dilated cardiomyopathy, megaesophagus, megacolon.

  • African sleeping sickness is caused by Trypanosoma brucei.

Exam Pearl:
American trypanosomiasis (Chagas disease) = Trypanosoma cruzi transmitted by the kissing bug.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৬) Which drug is used in AF patient with MS?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
In atrial fibrillation (AF) associated with mitral stenosis (MS), the primary goals are ventricular rate control and prevention of thromboembolism. Digoxin is a useful rate-controlling drug, particularly in patients with mitral stenosis who have heart failure or are relatively sedentary, because it slows AV nodal conduction by increasing vagal tone. Although β-blockers and non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (diltiazem, verapamil) are also effective for rate control, traditional examination questions commonly consider digoxin as the best answer for AF associated with rheumatic mitral stenosis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • AF + Mitral stenosis: Requires rate control + anticoagulation.

  • Digoxin: Useful for rate control, especially if heart failure is present.

  • β-blockers: Often preferred in active patients.

  • Warfarin is indicated for AF with moderate-to-severe rheumatic MS.

Exam Pearl:
In classic MBBS/FCPS MCQs, AF with rheumatic mitral stenosis is classically associated with the use of digoxin for ventricular rate control.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৭) Which is not a phase of specific therapy in acute leukemia?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The treatment of acute leukemia is divided into well-defined phases aimed at achieving and maintaining remission. These include remission induction, which eradicates leukemic blasts to achieve complete remission; remission consolidation (intensification), which destroys residual leukemic cells; and remission maintenance, particularly important in acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), to prevent relapse. There is no recognized phase called "remission termination" in standard leukemia treatment protocols. Therefore, this option is incorrect and is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Induction: Achieve complete remission.

  • Consolidation (Intensification): Eliminate minimal residual disease.

  • Maintenance: Mainly used in ALL; limited role in AML.

  • CNS prophylaxis is an essential component of ALL treatment.

Exam Pearl:
Acute leukemia treatment phases are Induction → Consolidation → Maintenance (especially ALL). "Remission termination" is not a treatment phase.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৮) Which one has high capacity of reabsorption?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) has the highest reabsorptive capacity of any segment of the nephron. It reabsorbs approximately 65–70% of filtered sodium and water, nearly 100% of glucose and amino acids (under normal conditions), and large amounts of bicarbonate, phosphate, and other solutes. This high capacity is due to its brush border (microvilli), extensive basolateral membrane infoldings, abundant mitochondria, and active transport mechanisms. In contrast, the loop of Henle, distal convoluted tubule (DCT), and collecting duct (CD) perform more selective and hormonally regulated reabsorption.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • PCT: Reabsorbs 65–70% of filtered Na⁺ and water.

  • Nearly 100% of glucose and amino acids are reabsorbed in the PCT.

  • Thick ascending limb: Reabsorbs Na⁺, K⁺, and Cl⁻; impermeable to water.

  • DCT: Site of PTH-mediated calcium reabsorption.

  • Collecting duct: ADH increases water reabsorption; aldosterone increases Na⁺ reabsorption.

Exam Pearl:
The PCT is the "workhorse" of the nephron, performing the majority of tubular reabsorption.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৯) A transferrin saturation of less than...... Is consistent with iron deficiency?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Transferrin saturation (TSAT) is calculated as:

TSAT = (Serum iron ÷ Total iron-binding capacity) × 100

In iron deficiency, serum iron decreases while total iron-binding capacity (TIBC) increases, resulting in a low transferrin saturation. A TSAT of less than 16% is classically considered consistent with iron deficiency anemia and is widely used as a diagnostic threshold in examinations. In clinical practice, a cutoff of <20% may also suggest iron deficiency, particularly in patients with chronic inflammatory conditions, but for standard MBBS and postgraduate MCQs, <16% is the accepted answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • TSAT = (Serum iron ÷ TIBC) × 100

  • Iron deficiency anemia: ↓ Serum iron, ↑ TIBC, TSAT <16%, ↓ Ferritin.

  • Anemia of chronic disease: ↓ Serum iron, ↓/normal TIBC, normal/↑ Ferritin.

  • Ferritin is the best indicator of iron stores.

Exam Pearl:
Remember: Transferrin saturation <16% is the classic laboratory cutoff for iron deficiency.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫০) Lyme disease is caused by.....?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Lyme disease is caused by Borrelia burgdorferi, a spirochete transmitted by the Ixodes (deer) tick. It is the most common tick-borne disease in North America and Europe. The disease typically progresses through stages. Early localized infection presents with erythema migrans, an expanding "bull's-eye" rash. Early disseminated disease may involve facial nerve palsy, meningitis, carditis (especially AV block), and migratory arthritis. Late disease commonly presents with large-joint arthritis, particularly affecting the knee. Diagnosis is based on clinical features and supported by two-tier serologic testing.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Causative organism: Borrelia burgdorferi (spirochete).

  • Vector: Ixodes (deer) tick.

  • Early sign: Erythema migrans.

  • Cardiac manifestation: AV block.

  • Late manifestation: Mono-/oligoarthritis, especially of the knee.

  • Treatment: Doxycycline (early disease); ceftriaxone for severe neurologic or cardiac disease.

Exam Pearl:
Lyme disease = Borrelia burgdorferi + Ixodes tick + erythema migrans ("bull's-eye" rash).

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫১) Which one corresponds to conjunctival xerosis in WHO classification of Xerophthalmia?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The WHO classification of xerophthalmia is used to grade the ocular manifestations of vitamin A deficiency. Conjunctival xerosis (dryness and loss of luster of the conjunctiva) is classified as X1A. It is often one of the earliest ocular signs of vitamin A deficiency. X1B denotes Bitot's spots, X2 represents corneal xerosis, X3A is corneal ulceration/keratomalacia involving less than one-third of the cornea, and X3B involves more than one-third of the cornea.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • XN – Night blindness.

  • X1A – Conjunctival xerosis.

  • X1B – Bitot's spots.

  • X2 – Corneal xerosis.

  • X3A – Corneal ulceration/keratomalacia <1/3 of cornea.

  • X3B – Corneal ulceration/keratomalacia >1/3 of cornea.

  • XS – Corneal scar.

  • XF – Xerophthalmic fundus.

Exam Pearl:
WHO Xerophthalmia mnemonic: X1A = Conjunctival xerosis; X1B = Bitot's spots; X2 = Corneal xerosis.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫২) What is the number of typical lumbar vertebrae?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
There are five lumbar vertebrae (L1–L5). However, typical lumbar vertebrae are L1, L2, and L3. These vertebrae share the classic anatomical features of the lumbar region: a large kidney-shaped body, triangular vertebral foramen, short and stout pedicles, quadrangular spinous process, and mammillary and accessory processes. L4 and especially L5 are considered atypical because they have structural modifications to bear greater weight and articulate with the sacrum. Therefore, the number of typical lumbar vertebrae is 3.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Total lumbar vertebrae = 5 (L1–L5).

  • Typical lumbar vertebrae: L1, L2, L3.

  • Atypical lumbar vertebrae: L4 and L5.

  • Lumbar vertebrae have large kidney-shaped bodies for weight bearing.

  • Spinous processes are short, broad, and quadrangular.

Exam Pearl:
Remember: L1–L3 are typical lumbar vertebrae, whereas L4 and L5 are atypical due to their weight-bearing adaptations.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৩) What is the percentage value of filtration fraction?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The filtration fraction (FF) is the proportion of renal plasma flow (RPF) that is filtered through the glomeruli. It is calculated as:

FF = GFR / RPF

In a healthy adult:

  • Glomerular filtration rate (GFR) ≈ 125 mL/min

  • Renal plasma flow (RPF) ≈ 625 mL/min

Therefore,

FF = 125 / 625 = 0.20 = 20%

This means that approximately 20% of the plasma entering the kidneys is filtered into Bowman's capsule, while the remaining 80% continues into the peritubular capillaries.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Filtration fraction (FF) = GFR / RPF

  • Normal GFR ≈ 125 mL/min

  • Normal RPF ≈ 625 mL/min

  • Normal FF ≈ 20%

  • Angiotensin II increases FF by preferentially constricting the efferent arteriole.

Exam Pearl:
Remember the renal physiology triad: RBF ≈ 1.2 L/min, RPF ≈ 625 mL/min, GFR ≈ 125 mL/min → Filtration Fraction = 20%.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৪) Which one is E shaped?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The erector spinae is the large intrinsic muscle group of the back that extends longitudinally from the sacrum to the skull. In cross-sectional anatomy, it is commonly described as having an "E-shaped" (or E-configuration) appearance because it consists of three longitudinal muscle columns: iliocostalis (lateral), longissimus (intermediate), and spinalis (medial). This arrangement gives it its characteristic appearance. In contrast, piriformis is a pear-shaped muscle, iliacus is fan-shaped, and multifidus is a deep segmental muscle without an E-shaped configuration.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Erector spinae = Iliocostalis + Longissimus + Spinalis.

  • Function: Extension and lateral flexion of the vertebral column; maintenance of posture.

  • Nerve supply: Posterior (dorsal) rami of spinal nerves.

  • Piriformis exits the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen.

Exam Pearl:
E-shaped muscle group of the back = Erector spinae (Iliocostalis, Longissimus, Spinalis).

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৫) Viridans group is normal flora of......?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The Viridans streptococci are a group of α-hemolytic streptococci that are part of the normal flora of the oral cavity and oropharynx (throat). Common species include Streptococcus mutans, S. sanguinis, and S. mitis. They play a role in dental plaque formation and are an important cause of subacute infective endocarditis, especially in patients with pre-existing valvular heart disease following dental procedures. Although they may be found elsewhere, their principal normal habitat is the mouth and throat. The skin is mainly colonized by Staphylococcus epidermidis, the vagina by Lactobacillus, and the urethra by mixed flora.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Viridans streptococci: Normal flora of the oral cavity and throat.

  • S. mutans: Major cause of dental caries.

  • S. sanguinis: Common cause of subacute infective endocarditis.

  • Alpha-hemolytic, optochin-resistant, bile-insoluble.

  • Differentiate from Streptococcus pneumoniae: optochin-sensitive and bile-soluble.

Exam Pearl:
Viridans streptococci are normal oral/throat flora and are classically associated with subacute infective endocarditis after dental procedures.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৬) Indicators used for measuring ECF volume excludes..?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Extracellular fluid (ECF) volume is measured using indicators that distribute throughout the extracellular space but do not enter cells. Common ECF markers include inulin, mannitol, thiosulfate, sulfate, bromide, and radioactive sodium. Antipyrine, however, freely crosses cell membranes and distributes throughout total body water (TBW), including both the intracellular and extracellular compartments. Therefore, it is not used to measure ECF volume but rather total body water.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • ECF markers: Inulin, Mannitol, Thiosulfate, Sulfate, Bromide, Na²².

  • TBW markers: Antipyrine, D₂O (deuterium oxide), Tritiated water (³H₂O).

  • Plasma volume markers: Evans blue dye, Radioiodinated albumin.

  • Blood volume = Plasma volume / (1 − Hematocrit).

Exam Pearl:
Antipyrine measures Total Body Water, not Extracellular Fluid volume.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৭) What is the most important point in sex differentiation of pelvis?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The subpubic angle (pubic arch angle) is the most important single feature used in sex differentiation of the pelvis. In females, the subpubic angle is wide (about 80–85° or more), facilitating childbirth. In males, it is narrow (about 50–60°). Although the shape of the pelvic inlet, pelvic outlet, and depth of the pelvic cavity also differ between the sexes, the subpubic angle is the easiest and most reliable anatomical feature for sex determination in osteology and forensic anatomy.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Female pelvis: Wide subpubic angle (>80°), oval/round pelvic inlet, shallow cavity.

  • Male pelvis: Narrow subpubic angle (<70°), heart-shaped inlet, deep cavity.

  • Female pelvis is adapted for parturition.

  • The greater sciatic notch is also wider in females.

Exam Pearl:
For sex determination of the pelvis, the most reliable single feature is the wide subpubic angle in females and narrow subpubic angle in males.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৮) Which is a cause of respiratory alkalosis?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Respiratory alkalosis results from alveolar hyperventilation, which causes excessive loss of carbon dioxide (CO₂), leading to a decrease in PaCO₂ and an increase in blood pH. Hysterical attacks (anxiety-induced hyperventilation) are a classic cause of respiratory alkalosis. Other causes include pain, fever, pregnancy, high altitude, pulmonary embolism, and early salicylate poisoning. In contrast, prolonged starvation causes metabolic acidosis (ketoacidosis), severe diarrhea causes metabolic acidosis due to bicarbonate loss, and alkaline drugs produce metabolic alkalosis, not respiratory alkalosis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Respiratory alkalosis: ↓ PaCO₂ due to hyperventilation.

  • Common causes: Anxiety (hysteria), high altitude, pulmonary embolism, pregnancy, fever, early salicylate poisoning.

  • Severe diarrhea → Metabolic acidosis.

  • Vomiting or alkaline ingestion → Metabolic alkalosis.

  • Renal compensation: Increased bicarbonate excretion.

Exam Pearl:
Hyperventilation is the hallmark of respiratory alkalosis; anxiety (hysterical attack) is the classic examination cause.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৯) Which one doesn’t take part in formation of conjoint tendon?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The conjoint tendon (inguinal falx) is formed by the fused aponeurotic fibers of the internal oblique and transversus abdominis muscles. It inserts into the pubic crest and pecten pubis, reinforcing the posterior wall of the inguinal canal medially and helping prevent direct inguinal hernias. The external oblique aponeurosis does not contribute to the formation of the conjoint tendon. Instead, it forms the anterior wall of the inguinal canal, the inguinal ligament, and the superficial inguinal ring.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Conjoint tendon = Internal oblique + Transversus abdominis.

  • Reinforces the posterior wall of the inguinal canal.

  • External oblique forms the inguinal ligament and superficial inguinal ring.

  • Weakness of the posterior wall predisposes to direct inguinal hernia.

Exam Pearl:
Conjoint tendon is formed only by the aponeuroses of the internal oblique and transversus abdominis—never by the external oblique.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬০) Wilms tumor associated gene is located at....?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Wilms tumor (nephroblastoma) is associated with mutations or deletions of the WT1 tumor suppressor gene, which is located on chromosome 11p13. WT1 plays a critical role in the normal development of the kidneys and gonads. Loss of WT1 function predisposes to Wilms tumor and is associated with syndromes such as WAGR syndrome (Wilms tumor, Aniridia, Genitourinary anomalies, and intellectual disability) and Denys–Drash syndrome. Another locus, WT2, located at 11p15, is associated with Beckwith–Wiedemann syndrome and is also linked to an increased risk of Wilms tumor, but the classic WT1 gene is located at 11p13.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • WT1 gene → Chromosome 11p13.

  • WT2 locus → Chromosome 11p15 (Beckwith–Wiedemann syndrome).

  • WAGR syndrome = Wilms tumor + Aniridia + Genitourinary anomalies + Intellectual disability.

  • Denys–Drash syndrome: WT1 mutation + nephropathy + gonadal dysgenesis + Wilms tumor.

  • Wilms tumor is the most common renal malignancy in children.

Exam Pearl:
Remember: WT1 = 11p13; WT2 (Beckwith–Wiedemann) = 11p15. This is a classic genetics MCQ.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬১) Which is abundant catecholamine?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The question is slightly ambiguous because it does not specify the site. In standard physiology MCQs, it is interpreted as asking about the adrenal medulla, where epinephrine (adrenaline) is the most abundant catecholamine, accounting for approximately 80% of catecholamine secretion, while norepinephrine (noradrenaline) accounts for about 20%. This predominance is due to the enzyme phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase (PNMT), which converts norepinephrine to epinephrine under the influence of cortisol from the adrenal cortex.

If the question referred to sympathetic nerve endings, the predominant catecholamine would be norepinephrine.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Adrenal medulla: 80% Epinephrine, 20% Norepinephrine.

  • PNMT converts norepinephrine → epinephrine.

  • Cortisol upregulates PNMT.

  • Sympathetic postganglionic neurons mainly release norepinephrine.

  • Dopamine is a catecholamine precursor and neurotransmitter.

Exam Pearl:
Adrenal medulla secretes predominantly epinephrine (≈80%), whereas sympathetic nerve terminals primarily release norepinephrine.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬২) What is the root value of nervi erigentes?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The nervi erigentes are the pelvic splanchnic nerves, which arise from the anterior (ventral) rami of the S2, S3, and S4 spinal nerves. They carry preganglionic parasympathetic fibers to the inferior hypogastric (pelvic) plexus, supplying the pelvic viscera. Their functions include contraction of the detrusor muscle, relaxation of the internal urethral sphincter, increased rectal motility, and vasodilation of erectile tissue, thereby facilitating penile and clitoral erection. Unlike other splanchnic nerves, the pelvic splanchnic nerves are parasympathetic, not sympathetic.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Nervi erigentes = Pelvic splanchnic nerves.

  • Root value: S2–S4.

  • Carry preganglionic parasympathetic fibers.

  • Supply: Hindgut (distal 1/3 of transverse colon onward) and pelvic viscera.

  • Function: Micturition, defecation, and erection.

  • Sympathetic supply to the pelvis: L1–L2 via hypogastric nerves.

Exam Pearl:
"S2, S3, S4 keep the penis off the floor"—Pelvic splanchnic nerves (nervi erigentes) arise from S2–S4 and mediate erection.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৩) Which is hormone of abundance?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Insulin is known as the hormone of abundance because it promotes the storage and utilization of nutrients when energy is plentiful (the fed state). It increases glucose uptake into skeletal muscle and adipose tissue, stimulates glycogenesis, lipogenesis, and protein synthesis, while inhibiting gluconeogenesis, glycogenolysis, and lipolysis. This anabolic effect allows the body to store excess nutrients for future use. In contrast, cortisol and adrenaline are stress hormones that increase blood glucose availability, while aldosterone regulates sodium and water balance.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Insulin = anabolic/storage hormone ("hormone of abundance").

  • Increases:

    • Glucose uptake

    • Glycogen synthesis

    • Fat synthesis

    • Protein synthesis

  • Decreases:

    • Gluconeogenesis

    • Lipolysis

    • Glycogenolysis

  • Glucagon = fasting hormone (mobilizes stored energy).

Exam Pearl:
Insulin signals the fed state and promotes storage of nutrients; therefore it is called the hormone of abundance.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৪) Which is the location of simple cuboidal epithelium?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Simple cuboidal epithelium consists of a single layer of cube-shaped cells and is commonly found in areas involved in secretion and absorption. The surface (germinal) epithelium of the ovary is lined by simple cuboidal epithelium. In contrast, the uterus is mainly lined by simple columnar epithelium, the fallopian tube has ciliated simple columnar epithelium with secretory cells, and the urethra is lined by different types of epithelium depending on the region (mainly pseudostratified/stratified columnar and stratified squamous near the opening).

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Simple cuboidal epithelium:

    • Ovary surface

    • Thyroid follicles

    • Kidney tubules

    • Small ducts of glands

  • Fallopian tube: Ciliated simple columnar epithelium.

  • Uterus: Simple columnar epithelium.

  • Urethra: Transitional/pseudostratified/stratified epithelium depending on part.

Exam Pearl:
Ovary surface (germinal epithelium) is a classic example of simple cuboidal epithelium.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৫) Radiation injury is not associated with....?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Radiation injury to the lung can cause several acute and chronic pulmonary complications. Early radiation-induced lung injury may present as radiation pneumonitis, which can lead to pulmonary edema-like changes and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) in severe cases. Chronic radiation injury may progress to pulmonary fibrosis due to persistent inflammation and collagen deposition. However, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is primarily associated with smoking and chronic airway inflammation, not radiation exposure. Therefore, COPD is not considered a typical complication of radiation lung injury.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Radiation lung injury phases:

    • Early: Radiation pneumonitis.

    • Late: Pulmonary fibrosis.

  • Severe radiation injury can cause ARDS.

  • COPD: Mainly caused by cigarette smoking and chronic airway inflammation.

  • Radiation fibrosis causes restrictive lung disease, not obstructive disease.

Exam Pearl:
Radiation damages lung parenchyma → pneumonitis and fibrosis; COPD is not a radiation-induced complication.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৬) Which hormone is called protein and carbohydrate sparer?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Growth hormone (GH) is called a protein-sparing and carbohydrate-sparing hormone because it promotes the use of fat as an energy source, thereby conserving glucose and amino acids for growth and tissue repair. GH increases lipolysis, decreases glucose uptake in some tissues (anti-insulin effect), and promotes protein synthesis by increasing amino acid uptake. This allows more amino acids to be used for growth rather than energy production. Insulin promotes protein synthesis but is primarily an anabolic and storage hormone, while cortisol increases protein breakdown and gluconeogenesis. Thyroxine increases overall metabolic rate but is not classically termed protein- and carbohydrate-sparing.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • GH: Protein-sparing + carbohydrate-sparing hormone.

  • GH effects:

    • ↑ Protein synthesis

    • ↑ Lipolysis

    • ↓ Glucose utilization (anti-insulin effect)

  • Insulin: Promotes glucose uptake and nutrient storage.

  • Cortisol: Increases protein catabolism and gluconeogenesis.

  • GH acts mainly through IGF-1 for growth effects.

Exam Pearl:
Growth hormone saves protein and carbohydrates by shifting the body toward fat utilization.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৭) Helicine arteries are present in which part of penis?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Helicine arteries are specialized branches of the deep arteries of the penis that are found within the corpus cavernosum. During erection, parasympathetic stimulation causes relaxation of smooth muscle in the trabeculae and helicine arteries, leading to increased arterial inflow into the cavernous spaces. Expansion of these spaces compresses the subtunical venous plexus, reducing venous outflow and producing penile erection. The corpus spongiosum also contains erectile tissue but does not contain the characteristic helicine arteries responsible for cavernous filling.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Helicine arteries: Present in corpus cavernosum.

  • Arise from: Deep arteries of the penis.

  • Erection mechanism:

    • Parasympathetic stimulation (S2–S4)

    • Nitric oxide release

    • Smooth muscle relaxation

    • Increased blood flow and venous occlusion

  • Corpus spongiosum surrounds the urethra and prevents urethral compression during erection.

Exam Pearl:
Helicine arteries of the corpus cavernosum are the key vascular structures involved in penile erection.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৮) ADH increases water permeability in all except...?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) increases water permeability mainly in the late distal convoluted tubule (DCT), connecting tubule (CT), and collecting duct (CD) by inserting aquaporin-2 water channels into the luminal membrane of principal cells. This allows increased water reabsorption and concentration of urine. The loop of Henle, particularly the ascending limb, is not affected by ADH because it is essentially impermeable to water. The descending limb is naturally water-permeable but does not have ADH-regulated aquaporin insertion. Therefore, the loop of Henle is the correct exception.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • ADH (vasopressin): Acts on late DCT, CT, and CD.

  • Mechanism: ↑ Aquaporin-2 insertion → ↑ water reabsorption.

  • Ascending limb of loop of Henle: Impermeable to water.

  • ADH deficiency → Diabetes insipidus.

  • Excess ADH → SIADH.

Exam Pearl:
ADH acts on the late DCT and collecting duct—not the loop of Henle.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৯) Which is an example of fibrocartilage?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Fibrocartilage is a tough type of cartilage containing abundant type I collagen fibers, providing high tensile strength and resistance to compression. The classic example is the articular disc (such as the intervertebral discs and temporomandibular joint disc). Other examples include the pubic symphysis and menisci of the knee. Costal cartilage is composed of hyaline cartilage, articular cartilage covering synovial joint surfaces is also hyaline cartilage, and epiphyseal cartilage (growth plate) is made of hyaline cartilage.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Fibrocartilage examples:

    • Intervertebral discs

    • Pubic symphysis

    • Articular discs

    • Menisci

  • Hyaline cartilage examples:

    • Costal cartilage

    • Articular cartilage

    • Epiphyseal plate

    • Tracheal cartilage

  • Elastic cartilage: Ear pinna, epiglottis.

Exam Pearl:
Fibrocartilage = intervertebral disc, pubic symphysis, and articular discs.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭০) Cell mediated autoimmune response occurs in.....?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Cell-mediated autoimmune response involves T lymphocytes, particularly CD8+ cytotoxic T cells and CD4+ T cells, causing tissue injury without being primarily mediated by antibodies. Coeliac disease is a classic example of a T-cell-mediated autoimmune disorder, where gluten (gliadin) triggers an immune response against the small intestinal mucosa, leading to villous atrophy and malabsorption. Acute glomerulonephritis (AGN) is mainly an immune complex-mediated (Type III hypersensitivity) disease. Polyarteritis nodosa (PAN) is also associated with immune complex deposition, while drug-induced lupus is mainly an autoantibody-mediated condition.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Coeliac disease: T-cell mediated autoimmune injury of small intestine.

  • Immune mechanisms:

    • Type II: Autoantibody-mediated (e.g., autoimmune hemolytic anemia).

    • Type III: Immune complex-mediated (e.g., AGN, SLE, PAN).

    • Type IV: T-cell mediated (e.g., contact dermatitis, TB, coeliac disease).

  • Coeliac disease antibody: Anti-tissue transglutaminase (anti-tTG) IgA.

Exam Pearl:
Coeliac disease is a classic example of a T-cell-mediated (cell-mediated) autoimmune disorder.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭১) T3=?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Triiodothyronine (T3) is formed by the coupling of one molecule of monoiodotyrosine (MIT) and one molecule of diiodotyrosine (DIT) within the thyroid follicular colloid. This reaction is catalyzed by thyroid peroxidase (TPO) during thyroid hormone synthesis. In contrast, thyroxine (T4) is formed by the coupling of two DIT molecules (DIT + DIT). T3 is the more biologically active thyroid hormone, with approximately 3–5 times greater activity than T4, although it is produced in smaller amounts.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • T3 = MIT + DIT

  • T4 = DIT + DIT

  • Enzyme involved: Thyroid peroxidase (TPO).

  • T3 is the more potent and active thyroid hormone.

  • Most circulating T3 is produced by peripheral conversion of T4 (mainly by 5′-deiodinase).

Exam Pearl:
Remember: T3 = One MIT + One DIT; T4 = Two DITs.

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭২) 1st metacarpal bone is example of…..epiphysis?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The 1st metacarpal bone is an example of an atavistic epiphysis. Atavistic epiphyses represent evolutionary remnants of bones that were independent in ancestral forms but have become fused with another bone during evolution. The epiphysis of the 1st metacarpal corresponds to the phalangeal component of the thumb, reflecting its evolutionary relationship with the digits. Other types include pressure epiphysis (articular ends bearing weight, e.g., head of femur), traction epiphysis (sites of muscle pull, e.g., greater trochanter), and aberrant epiphysis (occasional extra epiphysis).

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Atavistic epiphysis: 1st metacarpal, coracoid process, os trigonum.

  • Pressure epiphysis: Head of femur, head of humerus.

  • Traction epiphysis: Greater trochanter, tibial tuberosity.

  • Aberrant epiphysis: Occasional additional epiphysis not normally present.

Exam Pearl:
1st metacarpal epiphysis = Atavistic epiphysis (evolutionary remnant).

Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৩) What is the molecular weight of PTH?
Final Model Test-07 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Parathyroid hormone (PTH) is a single-chain polypeptide hormone consisting of 84 amino acids. Its molecular weight is approximately 9500 daltons (9.5 kDa).
